connectionDetails.notChecked: Tests the fixed public api.anthropic.com address without account credentials.
connectionDetails.readableResponse: A readable HTTP response was received. It describes this browser request only.
connectionDetails.httpWarning: An HTTP response was received, but indicates a restriction or temporary service issue. Compare it with the terminal report.
connectionDetails.opaqueResponse: The browser received an opaque cross-origin response. HTTP status cannot be read, so the result remains unconfirmed.
connectionDetails.requestUnconfirmed: The request could not be confirmed. Network, browser cross-origin policy, extensions or a timeout may cause this result.

claudeEnvironment.browserScope: A browser request cannot verify Claude Code proxy, TLS or login settings. No paid model request is made.

rtcDetails.notChecked: Enable the optional WebRTC check before starting.
rtcDetails.notRequested: WebRTC was not enabled for this run.
rtcDetails.unsupported: This browser does not provide an available WebRTC check.
rtcDetails.differentExit: A public candidate differs from the HTTPS exit. Review whether your proxy routing is as intended.
rtcDetails.sameExit: The public candidates observed in this run match the HTTPS exit. This does not guarantee the path of all traffic.
rtcDetails.publicOnly: Public candidates were observed, but the HTTPS exit is unavailable for comparison.
rtcDetails.localOnly: Only private addresses or mDNS names were observed. An additional public exit was not confirmed.
rtcDetails.noCandidates: No candidate was collected. Browser policy, network or extensions may block gathering; this is not proof that no leak exists.

claudeEnvironment.rtcScope: STUN and HTTPS may follow different routes. A difference is a diagnostic clue, not an account risk verdict.
claudeEnvironment.timeMismatch: Browser and exit-region timezones differ. Travel, remote work or proxy routing can explain this; check whether it is expected.
claudeEnvironment.localScope: Shown locally only. Language and timezone are not used to infer account eligibility or a ban probability.
claudeEnvironment.cliIntro: Browsers cannot read terminal proxy or certificate configuration. Review the downloadable script, run it in the terminal used for Claude Code, and import its report. Requires Node.js 18+ and curl.
claudeEnvironment.cliStep2: Run in the terminal used for Claude Code:
claudeEnvironment.cliStep3: Import the generated JSON. It is parsed locally and is not uploaded.

claudeEnvironment.customBaseUrl: A custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is present. The script tests the official Anthropic address, not the custom endpoint or provider.
claudeEnvironment.cliScope: curl inherits this terminal’s proxy environment, verifies TLS and disables .curlrc. The DNS check uses the local resolver and may differ from proxy-side resolution. Only configuration presence is reported; proxy addresses, keys and tokens are not printed. Claude Code may still use different process settings.

ccswitch.note: The manual example below uses OpenAI Chat Completions with /v1 in the Base URL. Follow the app’s documentation for other formats. Import links require your key and are generated in the signed-in API console; this storefront does not read or store it.

sub2api.description: Administrators with a Sub2API deployment can add a compatible NeedToken API key as an upstream and expose their own client endpoint.
sub2api.step1: Follow the official deployment guide to prepare the service and database, or open your existing admin dashboard.
sub2api.step2: Add an API-key upstream. Configure its endpoint, key and supported models for the selected platform, then run an account test.
sub2api.step3: Assign the upstream to a group, create a Sub2API key for your client, and use the endpoint supplied by that instance.
sub2api.note: Sub2API requires your own deployment. The fields below are upstream references; platform support, appended paths and protocols depend on your installed version.

cloudflare.description: Add NeedToken as a Custom Provider in your own Cloudflare account and route requests through AI Gateway.
cloudflare.step1: Open AI Gateway in Cloudflare and add a provider under Custom Providers.
cloudflare.step2: Use NeedToken / needtoken for the name and slug. Enter the root URL below and store the upstream key following the official BYOK guide.
cloudflare.step3: Use this provider in your own Gateway, then copy the request URL and authentication settings generated by Cloudflare.
cloudflare.note: The JSON contains fields for creating a Custom Provider. Its Base URL omits the final /v1; retain /v1/chat/completions in the client request path to avoid /v1/v1 upstream.

openclaw.description: Add a custom model provider in OpenClaw and run your assistant with the NeedToken API.

openclaw.step2: Set NEEDTOKEN_API_KEY in the OpenClaw runtime environment and merge the template into openclaw.json.
openclaw.step3: Choose the needtoken model, reload the configuration, and verify one request in the assistant.
openclaw.note: The download is a template to merge with your existing configuration. It uses openai-completions; agent tool calling requires support from both the model and upstream protocol.
